caption: The attach model priced: each cloud-delivered subscription lists at 20% of appliance list price per year and support at about 16%, support attach is roughly 100%, and Q2 FY2013 shipped more than 1.5 subscriptions per appliance.
The original land-and-expand grid: quarter-by-quarter repeat purchasing for the top 25 customers, who by Q2 FY2013 had bought 11.4x their initial order against 4.6x for all customers.
The first target operating model, set in 2013: 22-25% non-GAAP operating margin against 6.8% actual, with sales and marketing to fall from 43.4% of revenue to 30-33%.

The 2009 cohort decomposed: on a 1.0x initial purchase, subscription renewals added 0.85x, support renewals 0.90x and new expansion 3.55x, so renewals supplied roughly a third of the 5.3x repeat total.
Target model one year on: the same 22-25% operating margin, but the sales and marketing target moved out from 30-33% to 33-36% while actual spend stayed at 46.6%.
The account-coverage pyramid that sets the ceiling on the direct model: about 50 global, 2,000 major, 20,000 named and more than 150,000 commercial accounts, each on a different touch model.
Lifetime value by acquisition cohort with cohort sizes: the 2009 vintage reached 8.6x its initial order by FY2015, but each later and much larger cohort starts the same climb from 1.3x.

The recurring-revenue engine in three numbers: subscriptions per device rising 1.7 to 2.2, contract duration flat near 1.9 years, and renewal rates above 90% on subscriptions and about 100% on support.
The sales and marketing target is pushed out a second time, to 35-38%, while actual spend held at 45.8%; the 22-25% operating margin goal was left unchanged for a third year.

Firewall refresh economics: appliance lifespan is distributed across four to seven years, and about 65% of the 2009 install base had been refreshed by FY2016, generally onto larger boxes with larger subscriptions.
Attach measured per customer rather than per box: Threat Prevention at 88% and URL Filtering at 72% penetration, against WildFire 33%, GlobalProtect 10%, VM-Series 4% and Traps 1%.

How the sales force is paid, and what it therefore sells: most compensation sits on product plus the first year of subscription and support, multi-year is commissioned at a much lower rate, and renewals go to inside sales.
The install-base expansion claim, sized: applying the 2009 cohort 11.8x multiple to the 2010-2015 vintages implies more than $8bn of future orders, up from the $5bn claimed a year earlier.
The growth-and-profitability framework that replaced fixed targets: margin expansion is indexed to which growth band the company is in, with 100-200bp a year while revenue grows above 30%.
The hardware install base, valued at about $2.8bn of cumulative product billings by FY2017 - the base against which attached subscriptions, support and refresh orders are sold.
Product revenue against the appliance peer set on rolling six- and eight-quarter windows: Palo Alto growing 12.3%, Fortinet 11.9%, Check Point 2.8% and Juniper down 23%.
Nine cohorts side by side in FY2016 and FY2017, with cohort sizes: the 2009 vintage at 17.5x, the 2017 vintage at 1.3x, and every vintage stepping up year over year.
Network security appliance share from 3.4% in Q2 CY2012 to 14.0% in Q2 CY2017, past Check Point at 12.6% and Fortinet at 10.6% but still behind Cisco at 15.9%.
Revenue per customer of $41.3k against Check Point $10.3k, Cisco security $8.6k and Fortinet $4.6k - the platform claim expressed as wallet share rather than logo count.
Visibility before RPO existed: average contract length reached about 3.0 years and short-term deferred revenue covered roughly 45% of the next year's consensus revenue.

The stated acquisition playbook: acquired teams run their own plays for nine months, then the core sales force is leveraged to target a 30-40% and later a 100% improvement over the target's standalone plan.
The FY2022 targets set in 2019: about $6.0bn of billings and $5.0bn of revenue on a 20% three-year CAGR - the scorecard management would later grade itself against.
The speedboat go-to-market in numbers: 850+ specialist sellers added on top of a 3,200-strong core team, taking $1m accounts from 542 to 921 and $10m accounts from 18 to 43 in two years.
Management grades its own 2019 targets: FY2022 billings guidance of $6.6bn beat the $6.0bn goal, while operating margin at 18.5-19% came in below the 21.5% promised.

The form-factor transition quantified: software rose from 11% to 39% of firewall-as-a-platform billings in two years, with 55-60% targeted for FY2024 and only mid-single-digit product revenue growth behind it.
Deferred payment plans as a share of bookings climbed steeply from FY2020, and the outlined bars show how much higher reported free cash flow margin would have been without them.

caption: The addressable-market bridge management uses to justify serial acquisition: $19bn of firewall in 2018, $181bn across four categories in 2025 and $257bn including identity by 2028.

Platformization as the operating metric, with its definition in the footnote: about 900 platformizations, 120% net retention among platformized customers, and an FY2030 goal of 2,500-3,500 and $15bn of NGS ARR standalone.
Where the cash actually comes from: collections on deferred payment deals signed in earlier years supplied about 30% of FY2024 free cash flow, 40% of FY2025 and a guided 50% of FY2026.
Software passed 45% of trailing product revenue in Q2 FY2026 from 38% a year earlier, with software firewall ARR up about 25% and hardware revenue still growing about 10%.

Platformization after CyberArk and Chronosphere: about 2,280 counts across five platforms, roughly 120% net retention, 65% of NGS ARR from platformized customers, and the FY2030 goal raised to 4,000+ and $20bn.

The largest business at the latest reported quarter: more than $2bn of trailing firewall bookings, hardware NGFW bookings up about 40%, software firewall ARR up 25%, and SASE ARR of $1.6bn growing at twice the market.
